description:
Goal: validate and calibrate our internal physics model (RangeSpikeTrajectorySimulator) by running matching launch conditions through libgolf and overlaying both trajectory sets in the spike dashboard.

## What libgolf is
C++ library (GPL-3.0) that models full golf ball flight via numerical integration — aerial phase, bounce, and roll. Key structs: golfBall (position, velocity, spin, altitude), atmosphericData (temp, wind, pressure, humidity), GroundSurface. FlightSimulator steps through time (e.g. 0.01 s) until isComplete(), producing position at each step.
Repo: https://github.com/gdifiore/libgolf

## Integration options (pick one)

1. GDExtension wrapper (most embedded, hardest)
   Build libgolf as a shared library, write a GDExtension C++ shim that exposes a RunSimulation(LaunchParams) -> Array<Vector3> callable to Godot. Requires GDExtension SDK setup, CMake, matching ABI per platform.

2. Standalone CLI bridge (recommended for prototype)
   Build a small C++ CLI tool (libgolf-bridge) that accepts launch params as JSON on stdin and writes trajectory JSON to stdout. C# side spawns it via Process and deserializes output into List<Vector3>. Decouples build systems; no GDExtension needed.

3. Port physics to C# (GPL-free, most work)
   Translate the libgolf aerodynamics (drag/lift coefficients, Magnus effect) into a second C# simulator. Keeps everything in Godot, avoids GPL, but requires understanding and porting the full model.

## Input mapping (our model → libgolf)
- BallSpeedMph → convert to m/s velocity vector via launch angle + azimuth
- LaunchAngleDeg → vertical component of initial velocity
- TotalSpinRpm → spin rate on golfBall (backspin)
- SidespinRpm → lateral spin component
- AtmosphericData: use sea-level defaults for initial comparison (temp=20°C, pressure=101325 Pa, humidity=0.5, wind=0)

## Output integration
libgolf trajectory points → wrap as RangeSpikeShotTrace with a distinct color (e.g. dashed or lighter shade). Add a "libgolf reference" toggle in the spike dashboard so both traces render in the same top-down, side, and 3D tiles simultaneously.

## License note
GPL-3.0 means libgolf cannot be statically linked into a commercial binary without GPL-licensing that binary. The CLI-bridge approach (option 2) sidesteps this for runtime use; the GDExtension approach does not. Option 3 (port) has no GPL exposure. Confirm intended shipping context before committing to option 1 or 2.

## Acceptance criteria
- Same launch conditions (e.g. Mizuno 9i: 109 mph, 20.5° launch, 120 rpm sidespin) produce both our trajectory and libgolf's trajectory
- Both render in top-down and side-flight tiles with distinguishable colors/styles
- Carry and peak height values are labeled for both traces so divergence is immediately visible
title: Compare RangeSpikeTrajectorySimulator against libgolf reference model

description: Two confirmed bugs in the libgolf bridge, plus a model-difference question to investigate. 1) CONFIRMED UNIT BUG: BallState::fromLaunchParameters(speed_fps,...) expects feet/second, but bridge.cpp passes mph directly (109 mph treated as 109 ft/s = 74 mph). Fix: multiply by 1.46667 before passing. This alone shrinks the effective launch speed by 32%, reducing carry by roughly (109/159.7)^2 = 46%. 2) CONFIRMED PHASE BUG: sim.isComplete() fires after roll phase ends (ball fully stopped), so the bridge records the final resting position, not aerodynamic carry. Fix: detect aerial->bounce phase transition via getCurrentPhaseName() and snapshot carry at that moment. 3) OPEN QUESTION: Even after fixing these bugs, the two aerodynamic models (our simplified Cd/Cl vs libgolf's Alan Nathan empirical model) may diverge. Nathan's model uses Mach-number-dependent Cd; ours uses fixed coefficients. Need to run controlled tests (no spin, flat launch) to isolate drag model differences. 4) OPEN QUESTION: libgolf's fromLaunchParameters initializes BallState with spin=0 (default); spin enters via golfBall struct through GolfBallPhysicsVariables. Confirm that the spin is correctly applied to the simulation despite the BallState having 0 initial spinRate.
title: Physics divergence: libgolf vs OpenFairway trajectory prediction

description: Once a tile has been drag-moved, the resize handle in the bottom-right corner stops responding. Root cause: BeginInteraction calls MoveChild(panel, GetChildCount()-1), elevating the panel above the canvas-level resize handle overlays in sibling order. ZIndex=100 on handles is not sufficient to win input focus against the repositioned panel. Fix: after CommitInteraction, move all resize handles back to the end of the child list.
title: Tile drag-to-resize broken after drag-to-move

description: Top-Down Flight, Side Flight, and Shot Distribution panels scale their drawing to fill the full tile rect, distorting the aspect ratio of the data. E.g. a 90-yard carry with 5-yard offline deviation should appear narrow; widening the tile should not stretch the flight path sideways. Fix: letterbox/pillarbox the data viewport inside each plot panel using FitRect() so 1 meter == 1 pixel in both axes.
title: Plot panels distort data by stretching to tile bounds

description: Goal: validate our internal physics model against libgolf (C++, GPL-3.0, https://github.com/gdifiore/libgolf) by running matching launch conditions through both and overlaying trajectories in the spike dashboard. libgolf uses numerical integration with structs: golfBall (position/velocity/spin), atmosphericData (temp/wind/pressure/humidity), FlightSimulator (steps at ~0.01s). Three integration options: (1) GDExtension C++ shim — most embedded, requires GDExtension SDK+CMake, GPL exposure; (2) CLI bridge — libgolf-bridge accepts JSON launch params on stdin, writes trajectory JSON to stdout, C# spawns via Process, recommended for prototype, still GPL at runtime; (3) Port physics to C# — no GPL, most work. Input mapping: BallSpeedMph→m/s via launch angle, LaunchAngleDeg→velocity vector, TotalSpinRpm+SidespinRpm→spin components, sea-level atmos defaults. Output: wrap libgolf points as a second RangeSpikeShotTrace with distinct style, toggle in dashboard. License note: GPL-3.0 means options 1 and 2 require GPL-compatible shipping context; option 3 avoids this. Acceptance: same launch conditions (e.g. Mizuno 9i 109mph/20.5deg/120rpm) render both trajectories with carry+height labels so model divergence is visible.
title: Compare RangeSpikeTrajectorySimulator against libgolf reference model
